Response to Comments:
STATEMENT P
STATE SENATOR KURT FRANK
1. Since the submittal of the Draft EIS in June 1973 for the proposed Airport Spur, the Division of Highways has initiated abatement measures in order to effectively reduce the predicted noise levels to meet the federal noise standards. These measures include sound barriers as shown on figure 30 of this Final EIS and air conditioning of Hamlin Garland School. The detailed design of the sound barriers will be incorporated into the final construction plans for the project.
The dominant traffic noise source at Site 24 is Howell Avenue. The substantial decrease in 1990 traffic on Howell Avenue, as shown on page 67, will result in a noise reduction which will far outweigh the noise contribution of the Airport Spur. The resultant noise level will be below the 75 dBA federal noise standard for commercial areas.
Although one airline was on strike and runway 7R was partially closed during the period the noise measurements were taken, typical aircraft noise levels were measured in the vicinity of Hamlin Garland School on a day when aircraft did use runway 7R.
The information and extent of the results from the noise study are commensurate with the scope of the project. Therefore, a re-study is not warranted. Sections IV, V, and VI of this Final EIS have been expanded in the discussion of the noise study and related impacts and include the commitment to noise abatement measures.
